name: 03-rust-the-narrow-sum-and-the-limit-in-the-lessons-words
why: The first finding says the payments are added as u32 and only then widened, that the addition is where the total stops fitting, and that the sum must be made in a u64 from the first payment. That is the idea of the linked sentences, that a sum is only as wide as the type it is added in and that widening afterwards restores nothing, and it needs no pattern name: the sum is found. The second says a batch may hold up to limit_cents, so a payment that brings it exactly to the limit belongs in it, which is the idea of the linked sentence that a limit of at most n admits n: the comparison is found. The repeated-ids scan is not mentioned: missed.

key.consequence: A payment that would bring a batch to exactly the limit is moved into the next batch, so no batch is ever filled to the limit and more batches are made than are needed.
key.explanation: The check starts a new batch when the running total reaches the limit, but a batch may hold exactly the limit. Compare with > so that only a payment that would go over starts a new batch.

judged.reason: The edit changes > to >= in the check that starts a new batch, and the clean code lets a batch reach the limit.

sentences.text: A limit of at most n admits n itself: a value equal to the limit still fits.

key.consequence: The sum is taken in a u32, which overflows once the total passes about 4.29 billion cents: a debug build panics, and a release build wraps around to a small number that u64::from then widens unchanged, so a large batch reports a total far too small.

fix.before:
let total: u32 = payments.iter().map(|payment| payment.cents).sum();
    u64::from(total)

key.explanation: total_cents widens only the finished sum, after the u32 addition has already overflowed. Widen each amount to u64 first and sum in u64.

judged.reason: The edit sums the amounts as u32 and widens the result, and the clean code widens each amount before the sum.

sentences.text: A sum is only as wide as the type it is added in, so pick a type that holds the largest possible total before you start adding.
Widening a result afterwards cannot restore what has already wrapped or panicked.

key.consequence: For every payment the loop scans all the payments before it, so the work grows with the square of the list's length and a list of a hundred thousand payments takes billions of comparisons.
key.explanation: repeated_ids searches the earlier payments for every payment. Keep a HashSet of the ids seen so far, so that each payment costs one lookup.

judged.reason: The edit replaces the HashSet of seen ids with a scan of the earlier payments, and the clean code does one lookup per payment.

review.text: The payments are added up as u32 and only then turned into a u64. The addition is where the total stops fitting, so widening afterwards is too late; add in a u64 from the first payment.
A batch is allowed to hold up to limit_cents, so a payment that brings it exactly to the limit still belongs in it. This comparison sends such a payment to the next batch.
